evidence.title: Fourth Temporary Extension of COVID-19 Telemedicine Flexibilities for Prescription of Controlled Medications
Special Registrations for Telemedicine and Limited State Telemedicine Registrations (proposed rule)
Drug Enforcement Administration final rules (agency document list, queried for telemedicine, 2025-01-01 to 2026-09-14)

outcomes.note: No DEA final rule that sets a permanent telemedicine prescribing framework is in the Federal Register as of 2026-09-14. A Federal Register query of DEA rules for 2025-01-01 to 2026-09-14 returns only: the buprenorphine and VA continuity-of-care telemedicine rules of 2025-01-17 (narrow, drug- and population-specific, not a general framework), their delay rules, the Fourth Temporary Extension published 2025-12-31 that keeps the COVID-era flexibilities to 2026-12-31, and a SUPPORT Act medication-assisted treatment rule published 2026-06-09. The general framework exists only as the proposed rule of 2025-01-17. Its final version is still under review at OIRA. A temporary rule and an extension are not adoption. This states nothing about later dates.

evidence.title: Accelerated Intermittent Theta-Burst Stimulation and Treatment-Refractory Bipolar Depression: A Randomized Clinical Trial
Intensive TMS for Bipolar Depression (NCT05228457), posted results
Accelerated Intermittent Theta-Burst Stimulation and Treatment-Refractory Bipolar Depression: A Randomized Clinical Trial (PMID 38985492)

outcomes.note: University of Pennsylvania trial NCT05228457, a randomized, triple-masked, sham-controlled RCT of imaging-guided accelerated iTBS (SNT-type protocol: 10 sessions per day for 5 days, 90000 pulses) in treatment-refractory bipolar depression. The prespecified primary outcome was repeated MADRS before and after treatment. It met significance: active 30.4 to 10.5, sham 28.0 to 25.3, difference -14.75 (95% CI -19.73 to -9.77), P<.001, n=24 analysed. First public report: JAMA Psychiatry online, 2024-07-10; ClinicalTrials.gov results posted 2025-03-12. The criterion also requires a date after the statement date, which this resolver does not see. Two other candidates fail: the JAMA Network Open aiTBS bipolar RCT of 2025-02-11 missed its primary endpoint, and the BMC Psychiatry adolescent trial of 2025-12-22 used one session per day.

evidence.title: Ketalar (Ketamine) and Spravato (Esketamine), Community Plan Medical Benefit Drug Policy CS2026D0069AA
Ketamine for the Treatment of Psychiatric Disorders, Medical Policy 3.01.13
Coverage Policy for IV Ketamine Infusion Therapy for Major Depressive Disorder With or Without Suicidality, ForwardHealth Update 2024-53
Clinical Review Criteria: Ketamine for the Treatment of Depression and Other Psychiatric Disorders
evidence.publisher: Kaiser Foundation Health Plan of Washington

outcomes.note: No US health plan policy that lists IV ketamine as covered for bipolar depression was found in force on 2026-09-14. Checked: UnitedHealthcare Community Plan CS2026D0069AA, effective 2026-05-01, calls ketamine injection investigational for psychiatric disorders, and names bipolar disorder; Excellus BCBS 3.01.13, effective 2026-01-22, calls it investigational for all diagnosis codes; Wisconsin Medicaid (ForwardHealth Update 2024-53, effective 2025-01-01) covers IV ketamine only for major depressive disorder and refuses prior authorization for any other off-label indication, so it is excluded; Kaiser Washington criteria, last reviewed 2025-12-02, are non-coverage and record no Medicare NCD or LCD. The Ket-BD RCT published in JAMA Psychiatry in 2026 has not yet produced a payer policy. This states nothing about later dates.
